title: SPOILERS: Jailer 2 Ending Sets Up Jailer 3, Hrithik Roshan Cameo Confirmed
excerpt: Spoiler warning: two release-day reports and an independent review confirm Hrithik Roshan as Roddy and a Vijay Sethupathi closing scene pointing to a third film.
body:
• SPOILER: This article discusses the ending of Jailer 2, including a surprise appearance and the setup for a third film — stop here if you have not seen it.
  • Two separate reports published on release day confirm Hrithik Roshan appears as Roddy, who helps Rajinikanth's Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, and an independent review also singles out his appearance.
  • The closing scene features Vijay Sethupathi and, according to both reports, clearly sets up Jailer 3, unlike the first film, which ended without a sequel promise.
  • Jailer 2, directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Sun Pictures, opened in theatres worldwide on October 15.

Spoiler warning: Jailer 2 opened on October 15 with Rajinikanth back as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, and its ending has become the story. Reporting by Bollywood Hungama and a second release-day report by CineTalkers agree on the central surprise, and an independent review in Only Kollywood also calls out the same appearance.

The surprise appearance, verified in more than one report

Hrithik Roshan appears at a key point and helps Tiger, according to both Hungama and CineTalkers. Both name the character as Roddy and give the same backstory: Tiger helped him 20 years earlier, leaving him in Tiger's debt. Both also note that Hrithik speaks Tamil in the sequence. Only Kollywood's review, written separately from the news reports, describes Hrithik's appearance as a notable surprise alongside returns by Mohanlal and Shiva Rajkumar.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=5cXrSIKkhJ8

That overlap matters because pre-release speculation about star cameos in a Rajinikanth film is routine, and not all of it proves true. Here the character name, motive and placement match across two news reports, and the performance is also mentioned in a full review of the finished film.

The Chulbul Pandey nod and the Rajinikanth nod

Both news reports describe the same two visual jokes in the cameo. Hrithik tucks his sunglasses behind his shirt collar, a gesture audiences associate with Salman Khan's Chulbul Pandey in the Dabangg films. He also handles his sunglasses in Rajinikanth's familiar style, in front of Rajinikanth himself. Read together, the scene is staged as a meeting of three screen personas rather than a walk-on.

The first Jailer built much of its theatrical energy the same way, through Rajinikanth's performance, songs and a chain of star appearances. Jailer 2 extends that formula across industries: a Hindi film star entering a Tamil franchise, speaking Tamil, and borrowing mannerisms from both a Hindi and a Tamil icon.

How the film ends — and what it sets up

The first Jailer ended without signalling a sequel. Jailer 2 does the opposite. Hungama and CineTalkers both report that the final scene features Vijay Sethupathi and is designed to promise Jailer 3. Only Kollywood reaches the same conclusion in different words, saying the film ends with another star cameo that hints at a potential third chapter.

No production date, cast list or director confirmation for a third film was reported in any of the three sources. The promise, for now, is on screen, not in a studio announcement. Readers should treat talk of a Jailer 3 start date as speculation until Sun Pictures or Nelson confirms it.

What diaspora viewers need to know

Jailer 2 is in theatres now, released worldwide on October 15, directed by Nelson Dilipkumar with music by Anirudh Ravichander. The ensemble includes Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu, S. J. Suryah, Vidya Balan and Mithun Chakraborty, with Mohanlal and Shiva Rajkumar also appearing. If you plan to see it unspoiled, avoid social media clips of the final 20 minutes — the two moments described above are exactly the ones being shared.

For Rajinikanth fans in the US, Canada, the UK and the Gulf, the practical choice is simple: see it in its opening days if the ending matters to you, because this is a film whose last scene was built to be talked about immediately.
